narrative:
The model predicts a 90% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, the fact that you have received other job offers while working here, and the relatively short time you have spent in your current role. 

Your six to ten years of total professional experience pushed the prediction strongly toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have only one to five years of experience, your mid-level tenure matches profiles of people who often move on to new opportunities. Similarly, having received external job offers during your time here was a major driver toward predicting departure, as this is far less common among those expected to remain. Finally, spending just one to five years in your current organization also contributed to the "will leave" direction, since longer tenures in one place are more typical of employees the model expects to stay.

Taken together, these signals created a clear picture of someone ready for a change. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You may want to explore what would make staying more appealing, such as clearer advancement paths or better recognition of your experience. Addressing these areas could change the outlook for both sides. (248 words)
